original_sql:
SELECT c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty
FROM customer, orders, lineitem
WHERE o_orderkey IN (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 300)
  AND c_custkey = o_custkey
  AND o_orderkey = l_orderkey
GROUP BY c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice
ORDER BY o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate, o_orderkey
LIMIT 100

SELECT c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty
FROM customer
JOIN orders ON c_custkey = o_custkey
JOIN lineitem ON o_orderkey = l_orderkey
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lineitem li2 WHERE li2.l_orderkey = o_orderkey GROUP BY li2.l_orderkey HAVING SUM(li2.l_quantity) > 300)
GROUP BY c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice
ORDER BY o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate, o_orderkey
LIMIT 100
candidates.rationale: Replaces the IN subquery with an EXISTS correlated subquery, which can sometimes be more efficient if the optimizer chooses a semi-join strategy that avoids materializing the entire subquery result set.

candidates.sql:
SELECT c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty
FROM customer
JOIN orders ON c_custkey = o_custkey
JOIN lineitem ON o_orderkey = l_orderkey
JOIN (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 300) AS filtered_orders ON o_orderkey = filtered_orders.l_orderkey
GROUP BY c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice
ORDER BY o_totalprice DESC, o_orderdate, o_orderkey
LIMIT 100
candidates.rationale: Converts the IN subquery into a derived table join, allowing the optimizer to potentially materialize the filtered order keys once and join against them, which can be faster if the subquery result is small.
